text: Agile methodology is a popular way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Each morning, the team holds a quick standup meeting, where everyone shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any problems they face. Before a sprint begins, the team selects tasks from a list called a backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe a feature from the user’s perspective. This approach relies on iterative development, meaning the team improves the product step by step, gathering feedback after each sprint to make it better.
